method_note: All six source_url values were re-fetched independently with WebFetch; source_title was not trusted. For the two is_null_result rows I ran my own searches first (6 distinct queries for the quantum-gravity gap, 8 for the organizational-structures gap, all my own wording) and reached my own conclusion on each BEFORE opening research-log/searches/phase-3.json. The exact point at which I opened the producer's log is recorded in the two null findings below. I deliberately did not run engine/search.mjs, because it writes a search_log row and the reviewer brief forbids touching the database; WebSearch/WebFetch were used instead.

findings.evidence: Re-fetched https://www.stsci.edu/jwst/about-jwst/history/mission-timeline. The page states verbatim: 'From conception to launch of the James Webb Space Telescope took 32 years and the hard work and dedication of thousands of individuals.' The clock endpoints match the row: start 13-15 September 1989 NGST Workshop at STScI, end 25 December 2021 launch, which is exactly the as_of value. The quantity ('elapsed time from first concept study to launch') is what the source measures, not an adjacent quantity. target_value and target_basis are both NULL, so there is no invented round number to fail on, and the caveat states plainly that no agency publishes a target. Two minor observations, neither affecting the verdict. (1) source_checked is 'unchecked' although the page is fetchable and confirms the figure verbatim on the first try; the flag understates the row. (2) The context field says 'the ELT about 31' in the past tense alongside Rubin's completed 33. The ELT has not achieved first light (currently projected around 2029), so 31 is a projection presented in the same grammatical frame as two achieved durations. Worth re-wording if the context string is surfaced in the artifact.

Re-fetched https://www.osti.gov/biblio/2281696. The abstract states verbatim: 'Over 17 days of continuous operation, the A-Lab realized 41 novel compounds from a set of 58 targets including a variety of oxides and phosphates.' 41/17 = 2.41, so current_value 2.4 is correct. as_of 2023-11-29 matches the publication date exactly. No target_value, so no unsupported-target exposure. Note for the record, not a defect: 2.4 is a derived value, not a figure printed on the source page; the derivation is arithmetic from two quoted numbers and is stated transparently in the rationale, so it passes, but it is the one row where the number does not literally appear at the URL. The caveat honestly records the Palgrave and Schoop reanalysis contesting what counts as a novel compound, and the 'guess' confidence is correctly assigned for the numerator rather than as generic hedging — this is the row handling its own weakness best.

Re-fetched https://www.microns-explorer.org/cortical-mm3. Dimensions confirmed verbatim: '1.4mm x .87mm x .84 mm volume of cortex', which multiplies to 1.023 mm³, supporting current_value 1.0. Also confirmed verbatim: 'more than an estimated 200,000 cells, and 120,000 neurons' and 'Automated synapse detection measured more than 523 million synapses.' as_of 2025-04-09 matches the Nature publication date of the associated paper (Nature 640(8058):435-47). I separately verified the target_basis rather than accepting it: fetched RFA-NS-22-049, which states verbatim that the BRAIN Initiative Working Group 2.0 'called for a complete nanometer-level reconstruction of an entire mouse brain as a potential revolutionary project for the second phase of the BRAIN Initiative.' The target is therefore a real programme goal, and the row is explicit that the ~500 mm³ conversion is the producer's own approximation rather than the programme's wording — which is the correct way to record it. I also checked independently whether a larger synaptic-resolution dataset has appeared since April 2025; a 2025 Nature Reviews Neuroscience survey still puts the accessible ceiling at about 1 mm³ and describes whole-rodent-brain connectomes as the next target, so the row is not stale as of August 2026. This is the best-supported row in the set.

Re-fetched https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jamainternalmedicine/fullarticle/2702287. Confirmed verbatim: '$19.0 million (interquartile range, $12.2 million-$33.1 million)', 138 pivotal trials, 59 novel therapeutic agents, 2015-2016. I also independently verified the context figures, which are load-bearing for the artifact's 2.7x line: pivotal trials using a clinical outcome endpoint cost a mean of $64.7 million (95% CI $46.6-82.9M) against $24.0 million (95% CI $17.7-30.4M) for the 73 trials using a surrogate outcome. 64.7/24.0 = 2.70, so the '2.7 times' claim checks out. No target_value, correctly, and the rationale explains why it declined the tempting 2.5M publicly-funded-trials comparator — that reasoning is sound and I would not overturn it. Two corrections to the row's own commentary, neither changing the value. (1) The rationale asserts the publisher 'returns HTTP 403 to non-browser clients, so an automated link check flags it as unreachable'. That did not reproduce: my fetch returned the full article body including figures well past the abstract (uncontrolled trials $13.5M, controlled $35.1M, maximum $346.8M, minimum ~$2.1M). The 'verified' status is right, but the stated reason for it is not accurate and should not be published as a methodological note. (2) The underlying data is now roughly ten years old and is not inflation-adjusted. as_of 2016-12-31 and the caveat disclose this honestly, so it is not 'stale' in the protocol's sense, but any sentence in the artifact that reads this as a present-day cost should carry the date.

findings.target: gap_indicators id=13 — 1fccb37e-2a00-8071-859f-f25fac2df35c — contacted gate pitch 45 nm
findings.evidence: Graded strictly, as instructed. Re-fetched https://semiwiki.com/semiconductor-manufacturers/tsmc/322688-iedm-2022-tsmc-3nm/ (Scotten Jones, 2 January 2023). The value is confirmed verbatim: 'In the first paper, a Contacted Gate Pitch (Contacted Poly Pitch, CPP as I describe it) of 45nm is disclosed', along with the N3E 'minimum metal pitch of 23nm'. I also independently confirmed the target_basis quote is genuine and not paraphrased: the IRDS 2023 More Moore chapter does contain 'After 2031 there is no room for 2D geometry scaling, where 3D very large scale integration (VLSI) of circuits and systems using sequential/stacked integration approaches will be necessary.' So both the number and the roadmap quote survive. The row fails on currency, not on accuracy. reads_as makes a present-tense superlative claim — 'The tightest contacted gate pitch in volume production' — carrying as_of 2022-12-31. Since then TSMC N2 entered volume production in Q4 2025 (confirmed: C.C. Wei, 'N2 is well on track for volume production later this quarter, with good yield') and Intel 18A also entered production in 2025. I could not find any public CPP disclosure for N2 to settle whether 45 nm still stands, and at least one analysis states the opposite direction of travel: that N2's density advantage 'is derived from a tighter Contact Poly Pitch (CPP)'. So the superlative is a four-year-old claim about a two-node-old process, and it is currently unverified rather than merely undisclosed. Separately, and independently of staleness: target_value contains the string 'no further 2D geometry scaling projected after 2031' in a row whose unit is 'nm'. That is a date statement, not a value of the row's quantity. The basis behind it is real and verified, but a target that cannot be compared against current_value on the same axis does not do the job target_value exists to do. Recommend either re-dating the row and dropping the superlative, or scoping reads_as to 'TSMC N3, as disclosed at IEDM 2022'.

Graded strictly, as instructed, and it does not survive. The figure itself is real and appears verbatim in the source: 'This translates to an retraction rate of approximately 11.04 per 10,000 articles.' The problem is what it measures. The same paper states its scope verbatim as 'Between 2000 and 2024, journals indexed by SCI, SSCI, and ESCI published a total of nearly 42 million articles, of which over 46,000 were retracted' — so 11.04 is a twenty-five-year cumulative average, not a current rate. The source then says so explicitly: 'the retraction rate in 2022 was around 41, significantly higher than the average rate of 11.04'. The row presents 11.04 with as_of 2025-08-31 and reads_as 'About 11 papers in every 10,000 are eventually retracted', which frames a long-run average as the present-day rate that the source's own text puts roughly four times higher. That is precisely the failure mode the protocol names: a number that appears on the page but measures something adjacent. Three compounding errors, all traceable to one conflation. (1) The rationale states 'roughly 55,000 retracted papers give an overall rate of about 11.04 per 10,000 articles'. Those are two different figures from two different sentences: 55,000 is the corpus of unique retracted papers 'As of the end of August 2025', while the 11.04 numerator is the >46,000 retractions over 2000-2024. 55,000 over 42 million would be 13.1, not 11.04, so the rationale's own arithmetic does not reproduce its own number. (2) as_of 2025-08-31 is the date attached to the 55,000 corpus statement, not to the 11.04 rate, whose window closes at end-2024. The date is bound to the wrong figure. (3) The context field's discipline range, '0.035% in Physics to 0.34% in Computer Science' (i.e. 3.5 and 34 per 10,000), does not match the source, which gives 3.25 for Physics and 31.97 for Electrical Engineering, Electronics & Computer Science. Close, but these are stated to three significant figures in the source and were not read off it. The preprint status flagged in the brief is real (arXiv 2511.21176, v1 26 November 2025, v2 6 July 2026, and the row's source_title matches the v2 title while the cited figures are traceable to v1) but it is the least of this row's problems. Blocking because the gap is tiered 'Proxy only' and the artifact leans on this row to make a point about direction ambiguity; a current rate understated roughly fourfold is a wrong number in the artifact's mouth. The fix is cheap: re-date to end-2024, say 'average over 2000-2024', and if a current-rate reading is wanted, use the source's own ~41 per 10,000 for 2022 with its own caveat.

findings.target: gap_indicators id=15 — 1c1cb37e-2a00-8027-8eda-e6f4a472c3ad — asserted null, Quantum Gravity is Experimentally Hard to Constrain
findings.evidence: FALSE NULL. A usable quantitative indicator exists and the row asserts that none does. Sequencing, as required: I ran six independent searches of my own wording before opening the producer's log — (a) smallest source mass whose gravitational field has been measured; (b) largest mass placed in quantum superposition, matter-wave interferometry records toward Planck mass; (c) gravitationally induced entanglement required sensitivity roadmap, quantitative; (d) quantum gravity phenomenology figure of merit, benchmark, progress metric improving over time; (e) the one-milligram torsional pendulum result; (f) the definition and threshold of the resulting figure-of-merit. I then made two fetches to pin the numbers down. THE INDICATOR: the quantum-gravity figure-of-merit eta, defined as eta^2 = xi^2|grad F|/(h-bar omega_0), where xi is quantum delocalization, |grad F| the force gradient between the masses and omega_0 the angular frequency. It measures how close an experiment is to generating observable gravitationally-induced entanglement. Current value: eta = 2.8e-9, achieved by a 1 mg torsional pendulum operating at 18 Hz, laser-cooled from room temperature to 240 microkelvin — described as the highest quantum-gravity figure-of-merit benchmarked for a table-top experiment, ranking second only to LIGO. (The published version reports a refined value; I saw 2.8e-9 in the arXiv v2 full text and 4e-9 in secondary summaries of the journal version, so the exact mantissa needs reading off the final text — the order of magnitude, ~1e-9, is not in doubt.) Source: Agafonova, Rossello, Mekonnen and Hosten, ISTA — arXiv:2408.09445 (v1 18 August 2024, v4 20 December 2025), published as Communications Physics 9, 80 (2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.09445 and https://www.nature.com/articles/s42005-026-02514-w. Target: eta = 1, and this is a physical threshold rather than an invented round number — at eta^2 = 1 significant gravitational entanglement is generated within a fraction of an oscillation cycle. Direction: higher is better. The gap between current and target is about nine orders of magnitude, which is itself the finding, and is a direct quantification of the gap description's own words about 'the need for extremely large-scale or prohibitively expensive experiments' — eta is literally the axis on which a table-top apparatus is compared against LIGO. Crucially, Figure 3 of the paper benchmarks eta across roughly thirteen experimental platforms (nanospheres, membranes, cantilevers, microspheres, LIGO pendulums), which is what makes this a comparable indicator rather than a one-off number. WHY THIS OVERTURNS THE ROW: the rationale's stated ground for the null is that 'there is no agreement that any value of it settles anything about the gap: the community has no target, no direction of travel, and no shared claim about what a bound of 100 E_Planck would establish.' That reasoning is sound as applied to the Lorentz-invariance-violation bound the producer considered, and I would not overturn their rejection of the Fermi/LHAASO E_QG figure — it is the right call for the right reason. But the rationale generalises it into a universal claim about the field, and for eta all three of the missing ingredients exist: a target (eta = 1), a direction (higher), and a shared claim about what reaching it establishes (observable gravity-mediated entanglement, i.e. evidence that the gravitational field has a quantum nature). WHEN I OPENED THE PRODUCER'S LOG: only after the above was settled. It did not change my view, and it sharpened it. Their third query was 'tabletop quantum gravity gravitationally induced entanglement experiment sensitivity roadmap milestone' and their fifth was 'quantum gravity phenomenology figure of merit parameter constrained decade improvement' — nearly identical in intent to my (c) and (d). So the producer searched the correct neighbourhood twice and the eta paper did not surface in their result sets, while it surfaced in mine. This is therefore not a reasoning failure about scope; it is a search miss followed by a conclusion stated far more strongly than six queries can support. Their fourth query even returned 'Measuring gravity with milligram levitated masses' (Science Advances), which is the adjacent literature. Recommend replacing the null with an eta row, or, if the producer judges eta too specialised for the artifact's audience, rewriting the rationale so it rejects eta explicitly and on stated grounds rather than asserting that no such quantity exists.

findings.target: gap_indicators id=16 — 1c1cb37e-2a00-80b5-8cf4-c8195273fa45 — asserted null, Rigid Organizational Structures Constrain the Forms of R&D That Get Done
findings.evidence: NULL CORROBORATED, with one scoping objection. Sequencing, as required: I ran eight independent searches of my own wording before opening the producer's log — (a) share of federal research funding awarded through non-traditional mechanisms (OTA, cooperative agreements, ARPA-style), trend over time; (b) NIH average and median age at first R01-equivalent award; (c) researcher percentage of time on administration, Federal Demonstration Partnership faculty burden surveys; (d) metrics for diversity of research funding mechanisms and coordinated/team science; (e) the CD/disruption index decline; (f) Packalen and Bhattacharya on NIH funding of edge science; (g) quantified researcher time lost to unsuccessful grant proposals; (h) counts and total funding of Focused Research Organizations. I found no maintained indicator series that measures the quantity the gap is actually about — which forms of R&D get done and which do not. What exists is four kinds of near-miss, and each fails for a stateable reason. Administrative burden (FDP: ~42% of federally funded project time on administrative requirements; latest survey wave 2018, not a maintained series) measures inputs lost, not forms foregone. Grant-writing waste (NHMRC: 38 working days per new proposal, ~550 working years across 3,727 proposals at 20.5% success, Aus$66M; Horizon 2020: ~EUR 1.4bn of researcher time on unsuccessful applications) is a set of one-off studies, not a series. The disruption/CD index decline (Park, Leahey and Funk, Nature 613:138-144, 2023) is quantitative and dated but is an outcome measure, is not attributable to organizational structure, and is contested as an artifact of citation inflation. FRO counts (~8-10 launched) count experiments in institutional form, not the gap. So I independently reach the same conclusion the producer did, and by the protocol's own logic this makes the null substantially stronger: two agents searching with different wording both failed to find the quantity, and the 'Counterfactual required' tier is doing real work rather than excusing a thin search. WHEN I OPENED THE PRODUCER'S LOG: after the above was settled. It did not change my conclusion. Their six queries overlap mine at (c), (d) and the funding-RCT question; my (b), (e), (f) and (h) are additional ground they did not cover, and none of it turned up an indicator either. ONE OBJECTION, worth fixing before ship. The rationale dismisses the 42% administrative-burden figure on the ground that 'it measures one symptom of rigidity, not the quantity Convergent's sentence is about, which is which forms of R&D get done.' But Convergent's sentence has two clauses, and the first is 'scientists are spending a lot of time not doing science' — which is exactly what the 42% measures. The producer has scoped the gap to its second clause and then rejected a direct measure of its first. The null may still be the right call overall, since the FDP figure is not a maintained series and the gap's headline is about forms of R&D; but the rationale should not characterise the 42% as measuring something other than what the gap description says, because a Convergent reader will notice that their own sentence names it. ONE FURTHER CANDIDATE the producer did not consider at all: NIH's median age at first R01-equivalent award, 43 years across FY21-25, an official annually-maintained series published in the NIH Data Book and updated as recently as August 2026 (https://grants.nih.gov/news-events/nih-extramural-nexus-news/2026/08/age-at-first-r01-equivalent-award-remains-stable-since-fy21). It is a genuinely usable indicator on the protocol's mechanical criteria — current value, date, official source, direction, long back-series showing substantive increases through the 1990s and 2000s before plateauing. I do not think it should displace the null, because it measures career structure rather than which forms of R&D get done, and it is the same class of symptom as the 42%. But it is a stronger near-miss than either of the two the row currently names, and if the row is going to list its near-misses as evidence of search depth, this one belongs there.

Both null rows' rationales instruct the reader to 'see search_log, phase 3, this gap'. sqlite3 db/gapmap.sqlite 'select count(*) from search_log;' returns 0. The searches exist only in research-log/searches/phase-3.json, whose own note says that file 'is what makes the two null results provable rather than asserted'. So the two rows that most depend on provable provenance point the reader at an empty table. The evidence is real and I was able to audit it; only the pointer is wrong. Fix the rationale text to name the JSON path, or backfill search_log. Related and much smaller: source_checked is 'unchecked' on ids 9 and 13 while the other four read 'verified'; id 9's source verifies verbatim on a first fetch, so the flag understates that row.

The gate brief states the work is on branch 'review-gates'. git branch --show-current returns 'vercel-deploy-prep'. Reported rather than acted on, per CLAUDE.md's rule that unexpected branch state should be surfaced before merging rather than assumed. I made no git operations and wrote only this file.

summary: Four of the six numeric rows are confirmed against sources I re-fetched myself, and MICrONS is the strongest — I verified its target_basis verbatim in RFA-NS-22-049 rather than taking it on trust. Two must not ship as written: the retraction row presents 11.04 per 10,000 as a current rate when the source says plainly it is a 2000-2024 average and that the 2022 rate was around 41, and its as_of date and 55,000-paper arithmetic are attached to a different sentence of the paper than the rate is; the gate-pitch row's number and IRDS quote both check out, but its present-tense 'tightest in volume production' claim is four years and two production nodes stale. The load-bearing finding is on the nulls: the organizational-structures null is corroborated — I searched eight ways of my own and found no indicator that measures which forms of R&D get done, which makes that row genuinely persuasive — but the quantum-gravity null is false, because the quantum-gravity figure-of-merit eta (eta^2 = xi^2|grad F|/h-bar omega_0; currently ~2.8e-9 on a 1 mg torsional pendulum, threshold eta = 1, benchmarked across ~13 platforms, Communications Physics 9:80, 2026) has exactly the target, direction and shared meaning the rationale asserts the field does not have.
